![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14253263/assets/f25a56285499e3b2547e68bc57d4bbac3d79282c669f56e41d74de3394cb89c3.png)

Find the total area bounded by the polar curve $r=3\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta ),$ shown above.
question.worked_solution:
First, we want to find the interval for $\theta $ that corresponds to the first petal. Since the curve bounding the region crosses itself at the origin, we want to find the values of $\theta $ for which $r=0$, or 

$$
3\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta )=0.
$$

This gives us two solutions for $2\theta \in [-\pi ,\pi ):$

$$
2\theta =-\frac{\pi }{2},\frac{\pi }{2}\,⟹\,\theta =-\frac{\pi }{4},\frac{\pi }{4}
$$

As a result, the first petal is traversed for $-\frac{\pi }{4}\le \theta \le \frac{\pi }{4}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14253263/assets/6b70070505112ec0f12749b64937e3e0a8e8f72d77bfc1966a3edfb4c03c16b5.png)

Since there are $4$ petals, the total area bounded by the polar curve can be calculated as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{\text{total}} & =4\cdot {A}_{\text{petal}} \\  & =4\cdot \frac{9}{2}{\int }_{-\pi /4}^{\pi /4}{cos}^{2}⁡(2\theta )\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =18\cdot \frac{1}{2}{\int }_{-\pi /4}^{\pi /4}(1+\operatorname{cos}⁡(4\theta ))\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =9{(\theta +\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡(4\theta ))|}_{-\pi /4}^{\pi /4} \\  & =9[(\frac{\pi }{4}+\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi ))-(-\frac{\pi }{4}+\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡(-\pi ))] \\  & =9(\frac{\pi }{4}+\frac{\pi }{4}) \\  & =\frac{9\pi }{2}\end{aligned}
$$
